messages:
Priya Patel: FYI I just spotted a protobuf CVE that looks like it can affect our request deserialization path (CVE-2026-XXXX). It specifically mentions malformed varint handling in 3.20.x -> 3.20.1. Link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-XXXX

Devin Cho: thanks. do we know which services pull 3.20.x? runtime docker images? vLLM wheels?

Priya Patel: quick inventory: runtime image for hosted uses protobuf 3.20.0 via requirements-pin. vLLM wheel we build uses system protobuf on build image (3.20.0). FlashAttention kernels themselves unaffected but the glue layer that marshals configs between runtime <> vLLM could hit the parsing code.

Michael Ortega: can you paste the vulnerable stack trace or simple PoC?

Priya Patel: pasted minimal PoC from upstream: `\n```
# python PoC
from google.protobuf.internal import decoder
bad = b"\x08\xff\xff\xff\xff\0"
decoder._DecodeVarint(bad, 0)
```

This causes unbounded loop on some builds. Repro on py3.10 + protobuf 3.20.0 image.

Kevin (SRE): tagging KMS/audit question: any chance of secret exfil via this vector? i.e., could malformed payload trigger code path that logs request bodies or dumps keys?

Priya Patel: I ran a grep — we do not log raw protobuf payloads anywhere except job-debugging mode (disabled in prod). KMS keys are accessed via client libs after auth; no evidence the vulnerable code touches KMS material directly. Still, we should assume partial exploit could lead to process compromise.

sec-bot: Severity suggestion: CVSS 7.5 (High) based on remote parsing -> potential DoS/exec chain. Recommend expedited patch.

Devin Cho: proposed plan: (1) bump protobuf to 3.20.2+ in all runtime images and build images, (2) rebuild vLLM wheels on patched builder, (3) run full inference smoke and fuzz tests, (4) canary deploy to Dedicated pool, (5) monitor errors/latency and promote.

Michael Ortega: add: run the existing model-compat E2E for streaming & KV-cache; those paths exercise the parser extensively. I can own test harness.

Kevin (SRE): RBAC/audit items: tighten the package-builder role so it cannot access production KMS keys during wheel builds. Also rotate the build signing key for containers after deploy. I will open the RBAC PR and add audit retention to 180d for build logs.

Priya Patel: timeline? want to avoid breaking hosted customers, so canary on Dedicated first, then hosted. If tests pass, targeted Hosted API rollout with traffic shift 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 1-2 hours. Rollback policy: immediate rollback to prior image if any 5xx spike >0.5% or latency P95 regresses >15%.

Devin Cho: question about Triton/vLLM: Triton versions unaffected per advisory, but we should recompile FlashAttention kernels against patched protobuf build environment to be safe. That requires a quick rebuild of the wheel. Estimate 2-3h for CI+verification.

Michael Ortega: I'll run fuzzing job (model-runner-fuzz) against new builds overnight. If no crash after 50k iterations, green for canary.

Kevin (SRE): I'll prepare an automated canary job: `deploy-bot canary --service inference-runtime --image rwinf/runtime:proto-3.20.2-canary --pool dedicated-canary` and hook alerts.

Priya Patel: owners: Priya (lead triage & release plan), Devin (patch PR + build updates), Michael (tests & fuzz), Kevin (RBAC, KMS rotation, canary). Target: merge PR within 24h, canary deploy within 36h, full rollout in 48-72h unless blockers.

Devin Cho: starting PR now. ping me if you need package pins. I will include backports for any long-lived branches (v1-runtime-support).

Priya Patel: thanks all. please react with :thumbsup: when you pick up your action. Logging this thread for postmortem if anything regresses.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary job created: job id cj-83921. Will post status here when jobs start.
